summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma and a history of recurrent cholangitis, was admitted with right upper quadrant abdominal pain and low-grade fever. Imaging revealed an enlarging liver abscess, and he was started on meropenem. Due to prior ERCP-related bleeding, biliary intervention was avoided. Percutaneous abscess drainage yielded multidrug-resistant E. coli, resistant to his home suppressive antibiotics. He was transitioned to ceftazidime/avibactam and metronidazole. A new portal vein thrombus was identified and treated with anticoagulation using apixaban. Ursodiol was initiated to address biliary sludge. His infection resolved, and he was discharged with a PICC line for continued IV antibiotics, outpatient follow-up, and a plan for 4–6 weeks of antimicrobial therapy.
